target.title: fix(agents): stop inflating subagent spawn depth from /new rollover
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated `/new` in the TUI silently inflates subagent spawn depth, making `sessions_spawn` permanently unavailable after a single rollover. `parentSessionKey` — a session lineage field set by both `/new` rollover and subagent spawn — was incorrectly consumed as subagent nesting evidence. The fix restricts depth derivation to `spawnedBy` (explicit subagent lineage); `/new` sessions without subagent markers now correctly report depth 0.

- Problem: `getSubagentDepthFromSessionStore` falls back to `parentSessionKey` when `spawnedBy` is absent. `/new` sets `parentSessionKey` but is session rollover, not subagent nesting.
- Solution: Stop following `parentSessionKey` in depth derivation. Only `spawnedBy` and explicit `spawnDepth` drive subagent depth.
- What changed: `src/agents/subagent-depth.ts` (depth derivation), `src/agents/subagent-depth.test.ts` (tests updated + new `/new` chain test)
- What did NOT change: Spawned subagent depth — `subagent-spawn.ts` already sets `spawnedBy` and `spawnDepth` on child session entries, so their depth is unaffected.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #110577
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Report #110577: with `maxSpawnDepth: 1` (the default), a single `/new` makes `sessions_spawn` unreachable because the depth calculation treats `parentSessionKey` chain as subagent nesting. Each `/new` adds +1 to the caller depth. Since `DEFAULT_SUBAGENT_MAX_SPAWN_DEPTH` is 1, the very first `/new` already puts `callerDepth (1) >= maxSpawnDepth (1)`, permanently blocking subagent use. This is a P1 regression introduced by TUI lifecycle hooks (#100241) that started persisting `parentSessionKey` on `/new` rollover.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: `/new` no longer inflates subagent spawn depth. `parentSessionKey`-only sessions correctly report depth 0.
- Real environment tested: Linux x64, Node 22.22.3, branch `fix/subagent-spawn-depth-inflation-110577`

- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/subagent-depth.test.ts --run
```

- Evience after fix:

```console
$ npx vitest run src/agents/subagent-depth.proof.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts --reporter=verbose

 RUN  v4.1.10 /media/vdb/code/github/openclaw

stdout | src/agents/subagent-depth.proof.test.ts > subagent depth — real behavior proof > parentSessionKey chain alone does not inflate depth
  main (no parent):              0  | expected 0
  after 1x /new (parentSessionKey): 0  | expected 0
  after 3x /new (parentSessionKey): 0  | expected 0
  spawned subagent (spawnedBy):     1  | expected 1

 ✓ |agents| ... > parentSessionKey chain alone does not inflate depth

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

**Note**: The proof test calls `getSubagentDepthFromSessionStore` (the same function used by the spawn validation paths) directly with real production session entries, exercising the exact code path that determines spawn permission at runtime. The terminal output above is from the actual production code after the fix — no mocks, no stubs.

**Matrix-style evidence — depth by session type (before vs after)**:

| Session type | Before (depth) | After (depth) | Correct |
|---|---|---|---|
| Main session (`agent:main:tui-xxx`) | 0 | 0 | ✓ |
| 1× `/new` (`parentSessionKey` chain) | 1 | 0 | ✓ |
| 3× `/new` (`parentSessionKey` chain) | 3 | 0 | ✓ |
| Spawned subagent (`agent:main:subagent:flat`, has `spawnedBy`) | 1 | 1 | ✓ |
| Spawned subagent, depth 2 (has `spawnDepth: 2`) | 2 | 2 | ✓ |
| Dashboard child with `parentSessionKey` only | 1 | 0 | ✓ (not a subagent) |

- Observed result after fix:
  1. `/new` sessions now report depth 0, allowing `sessions_spawn` to work after rollover
  2. Spawned subagent depth unchanged (verified by both the spawned subagent depth-limits tests and `subagent-spawn` test suite)
  3. All 17 existing tests pass
- What was not tested: Live TUI gateway repro (logic-only fix; test coverage validates the invariant directly)
- **Fix completeness pre-check (4 questions)**:
  - ✅ Auth guard: N/A — pure internal logic, no policy/permission surface
  - ✅ Enum completeness: Parent chain covers all variants (`spawnedBy` set → follow; `spawnDepth` set → return directly; neither → depth 0)
  - ✅ Path coverage: All 6 call sites of `getSubagentDepthFromSessionStore` verified — all correctly get depth 0 for non-subagent sessions
  - ✅ Cleanup symmetry: N/A — no state/listener lifecycle

## Root Cause

`src/agents/subagent-depth.ts:160-161` follows `parentSessionKey` when `spawnedBy` is absent:

```typescript
// Before:
const parentKey =
    normalizeOptionalString(entry?.spawnedBy) ?? normalizeOptionalString(entry?.parentSessionKey);
```

Both `/new` (via `session-create-service.ts:676`) and subagent spawn (via `sessions-spawn-visible.ts`) set `parentSessionKey`, but only the spawn flow sets `spawnedBy` (via `subagent-spawn.ts:300-301`). The `/new` sessions had no `spawnedBy`, causing the depth calculator to walk the rollover chain and incorrectly add +1 per hop.

**Provenance**:
- Introduced by: `e905a682f7a` (feat(agents): session self-service tools) — original `parentSessionKey` fallback in subagent-depth.ts
- Made visible by: `cd305b3b0cb` fix(tui): run new sessions through lifecycle hooks (#100241) — TUI `/new` started persisting `parentSessionKey`
- Confidence: clear

## Regression Test Plan

`subagent-depth.test.ts` covers:
1. Direct `spawnDepth` → correct depth
2. `spawnedBy` ancestry → correct depth
3. `parentSessionKey`-only chain (new `/new` test) → depth 0
4. Cross-agent `parentSessionKey` without `spawnedBy` → depth 0
5. SessionId-based resolution → correct depth

Subagent spawn integration tests (`subagent-spawn.depth-limits.test.ts`) confirm spawned subagent depth is unchanged.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

`/new` no longer blocks `sessions_spawn`. Users with `maxSpawnDepth: 1` (default) can use subagents after `/new`.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Unit test suite (17 tests) covering all depth derivation paths
- Edge cases checked: `/new` chain (3-hop), cross-agent parentSessionKey, spawned subagent with spawnedBy, explicit spawnDepth
- What you did NOT verify: Live TUI gateway run (logic-only change; tests exercise the exact surface)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only fixes incorrect depth inflation for non-subagent sessions
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. The depth derivation boundary is the correct fix point — spawned subagents already carry `spawnedBy` (set by `subagent-spawn.ts`), so no protocol or storage changes are needed. Fixing at the consumer side avoids touching the session creation protocol (`sessions.create`) which cannot distinguish `/new` from spawn.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: Setting `spawnDepth: 0` on `/new` sessions in `session-create-service.ts`. Rejected because the same code path serves both `/new` and spawned sessions; the consumer-side fix is narrower.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: `Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>`
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: `/open-source-pr` skill workflow — issue selection, root-cause analysis, self-critical evaluation, implementation, and verification

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Subagent sessions that rely on `parentSessionKey` for depth when `spawnedBy` is absent.
**Mitigation**: `subagent-spawn.ts` always sets both `spawnedBy` and `spawnDepth` on child entries (`line 290-301`). The risk is theoretical – no production path stores a subagent session entry with `parentSessionKey` but without `spawnedBy`. Verified by reading the spawn entry construction code and by the passing depth-limits integration test.
**Compatibility**: No breaking changes. Only incorrect depth inflation is removed.

---

Fixes #110577
